item.title: States are pushing Medicaid beyond its intended limits
item.description: Medicaid, which covers roughly 76 million people, was originally designed as a safety-net program for the nation’s poorest citizens. Expanding it indefinitely, especially through legal gray areas and fiscal workarounds, risks undermining its fiscal future.

item.title: LAX People Mover Is Yet Another Infrastructure Failure In CA
item.description: It’s just another example of incompetent execution of infrastructure projects in California. The state has come a long way — in the wrong direction — since the 1950s and 1960s, when governments saw building as a feature rather than a bug.

item.title: Building more is the key to affordability
item.description: There is a bright spot, though, in San Diego. There, apartment construction is booming at the same time rents have fallen for the first time in 15 years. And it’s happened without a policy preoccupation on affordability. There’s a lesson here, if lawmakers are open to learning it.

item.title: California Can’t Address Affordability Crisis Without Lowering Tax Burden
item.description: Affordability is a buzz word for California’s gubernatorial candidates. Most of their ideas to promote affordability will do the opposite.

item.title: America’s Healthcare System Has Never Been Better At Keeping Patients Alive
item.description: Americans are living longer lives because our market-oriented healthcare system rewards innovation and attracts investment in medical science. Weakening those incentives through drug price controls may lower costs in the short term—but will mean shorter lives in the long run.

item.title: Washington Is Targeting the Wrong Culprit on Drug Prices
item.description: Blaming patents for high drug prices may be politically convenient. But it leaves PBMs free to continue distorting the market -- and risks undermining the very engine of progress in health care that allows patients to live longer lives.

item.title: Addressing California's Insurance Crisis
item.description: From PRI’s 2026 California Ideas in Action Conference, hear Free Cities Center director Steven Greenhut moderate a panel with some of the state’s top policy insiders and elected officials exploring the ongoing challenges facing Californias insurance industry, which were exacerbated by last year’s Southern California wildfires.

item.title: California Should Get Out of the Way of the Charter-Cox Merger
item.description: The foundation of any honest merger analysis is whether the combining parties actually compete with each other. In this case, they barely do.
